"Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 108, verse 1:"

He (ﷺ) was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is a river that my Lord has given me in Paradise. It is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and in it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels."

It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed they are delicate (naʿimah)." He said: "What they eat is more delicate than them."

(Section)

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the narration of Hammam, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"While I was walking in Paradise, suddenly there was a river whose banks were domes of pearl and hollow (al-mujawwaf). I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?'

He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which your Lord has given you.' He said: The angel then struck the ground with his hand, and behold, it was clay of musk, very fragrant (adhfar)."

In Sahih Muslim, from the narration of al-Mukhtar ibn Falfal, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said:

"Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, which my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has promised me."

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari said: Hadathana Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"I entered Paradise, and behold, there was a river flowing whose banks were tents of pearl. I struck my hand into what flowed in it of water, and behold, it was musk, very fragrant. I said: 'For whom is this, O Jibril?'

He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given you.'"

Al-Tirmidhi said: Hadathana Hannad, hadathana Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its banks are of gold, its course is over pearls and rubies, its soil is better than musk, its water is sweeter than honey and whiter than snow."

He said: This is a hadith that is hasan sahih.

Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl said: Hadathana Abu Ja'far, he is al-Razi, hadathana Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ [108:1].

He said: "Abundant good."

Anas ibn Malik said: "It is a river in Paradise."

And Aisha said: "It is a river in Paradise; no one puts his two fingers in his ears except that he hears the rushing sound of that river."

And its meaning, and Allah knows best, is that the rushing sound of that river resembles the sound that one hears when he puts his two fingers in his ears.

(Section)

Know that the coming of people to the Basin (al-Hawd) and their drinking from it on the Day of the Greatest Thirst is in accordance with their coming to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and their drinking from it. Whoever came to it in this abode, drank from it and quenched his thirst fully, will come there to his Basin, drink from it and quench his thirst fully. So he (ﷺ) has two great basins: a basin in this world, which is his Sunnah and what he brought, and a basin in the Hereafter. Those who drink from this basin in this world are those who drink from his Basin on the Day of Resurrection. So there is a drinker, a deprived one, one who drinks little, and one who drinks abundantly. Those whom he and the angels will drive away from his Basin on the Day of Resurrection are those who used to drive away themselves and their followers from his Sunnah, and preferred other things over it. Whoever is thirsty for his Sunnah in this world and has no drink from it, he will be in the Hereafter more thirsty and with a more burning liver. A man will meet another man and say: "O so-and-so, did you drink?" He will say: "Yes, by Allah." He will say: "But I, by Allah, have not drunk, woe to my thirst!"

So come forward, O thirsty one, and the coming is possible. If you do not come, know that you are lost. And if Ridwan does not give you a sip to drink, he will give it to you while you are thirsty, the Owner (Malik) will. And if you do not come to his Basin in this abode, you will be turned away from it on the Day when you meet Him (ānik).

(Benefit)

"Anas asked him (ﷺ) to intercede for him. He said: 'I will do so.' He said: 'Where shall I seek you on the Day of Resurrection?' He said: 'Seek me first at the Sirat.' I said: 'If I do not meet you at the Sirat?' He said: 'Then I am at the Scale.' I said: 'If I do not meet you at the Scale?' He said: 'Then I am at the Basin. I do not miss these three stations on the Day of Resurrection.'" Ahmad recorded both of these.

(Section)

His saying "then you will look upon the Basin of your Prophet" — the apparent meaning of this is that the Basin is beyond the Bridge, so they do not reach it until they cross the Bridge. Regarding this, the early scholars (al-Salaf) had two opinions, which al-Qurtubi in his "Tadhkirah" and al-Ghazali related, and they considered wrong the one who said it is after the Bridge. Al-Bukhari narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While I am standing at the Basin, suddenly a group appears, and when I recognized them, a man came out from between me and them and said to them: 'Come!' I said: 'Where to?' He said: 'To the Fire, by Allah!' I said: 'What is their state?' He said: 'They turned back on their heels, and I do not think any of them will escape except like the straying of camels (hamal al-naʿam).'"

He said: This hadith, with its authenticity, is the strongest evidence that the Basin is in the place of standing before the Sirat, because the Sirat is only a bridge stretched over Hell, and whoever crosses it is saved from the Fire.

I say: There is no contradiction, no conflict, and no difference among the hadiths of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); all his hadith confirm one another. As for the proponents of this view, if they mean that the Basin is not seen and is not reached except after crossing the Sirat, then this hadith of Abu Hurayrah and others refutes their view. And if they mean that when the believers pass over the Sirat and cross it, the Basin appears to them and they drink from it, then this is indicated by the hadith of Luqayt, and it does not contradict its being before the Sirat, for his saying that its length is a month and its width is a month. When it has this length and breadth, what prevents its extension beyond the Bridge, so that the believers come to it both before and after the Sirat? This is within the realm of possibility, and its occurrence depends on the report of the Truthful One, and Allah knows best.

His saying "by Allah, more thirsty than any group ever (ʿala aẓmaʾ nahilah qaṭṭ)" — al-nahilah are the thirsty ones who come to water, meaning they come to it in the greatest thirst they have ever known. This suits being after the Sirat, for it is the Bridge of the Fire and they have all come to it; when they have crossed it, their thirst for water intensifies, so they come to his Basin (ﷺ) just as they came to it at the station of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 108, verse 2:

ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said regarding the words of the Exalted, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: it means placing the right hand upon the left during prayer, beneath the chest. Ibn Abī Shaybah reported from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq that when he stood for prayer he would say, "Thus," and would place the right hand upon the left during prayer. Abū al-Dardāʾ said: Placing the right hand upon the left during prayer is among the manners of the prophets.

Others said regarding His words, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, that what is meant is: place your hand upon your throat (nahr).

Another, being overly clever, said the meaning is: face the qiblah with your throat.

Thus they overlooked the meaning of this verse, which combines the two great acts of worship: prayer and sacrifice (nusuk).

[Section: His Guidance Regarding the Sacrificial Animals (al-Udhiyah)]

Section. As for his guidance regarding sacrificial animals: the Prophet (ﷺ) never abandoned the udhiyah (sacrifice), and he would sacrifice two rams, slaughtering them after the ʿEid prayer. He informed that "whoever slaughters before the prayer, it is not part of the rite (nusuk) at all; it is merely meat he has brought forward for his family." This is what his Sunnah and guidance indicate, not the consideration of the time of the prayer and the sermon, but the act of sacrifice itself. This is what we hold ourselves to before Allah. "And he commanded them to slaughter the jadhaʿ of the sheep and the thaniyy of other than it."

That is, the musinnah (an animal of the age required).

It is also narrated from him that he said: "All the days of tashriq are days of slaughter," but the hadith is interrupted (munqaṭiʿ) and its connection (wasl) is not established.

As for his prohibition of storing the flesh of sacrificial animals beyond three days, it does not indicate that the days of slaughter are only three; for the hadith is evidence of the prohibition on the one slaughtering from storing anything beyond three days from the day of his slaughter. So if he delayed the slaughter until the third day, it would be permissible for him to store during the time of the prohibition what lies between that and three days. Those who limited it to three understood from his prohibition of storing beyond three that its first day is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr). They said: It is not permissible for slaughter to be legislated at a time when eating is forbidden. They said: Then the prohibition on eating was abrogated (nusikha), so the time of slaughter remained as it was.

It is said to them: The Prophet (ﷺ) only prohibited storing beyond three; he did not prohibit sacrificing after three. So where is one of them in relation to the other? There is no necessary connection between what he prohibited and the restriction of slaughter to three, for two reasons.

The first: slaughter is valid on the second and third days, so it is permissible for him to store up to the completion of three days from the day of slaughter. Your argument is not complete until it is established that slaughter after the day of sacrifice is prohibited, and you have no way to that.

The second: if he slaughtered in the last part of the day of sacrifice, then storage for three days after it would be permissible for him according to the hadith. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The days of sacrifice are the day of al-Aḍḥā and three days after it. This is also the position of the imam of the people of Basra, al-Ḥasan; the imam of the people of Makkah, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ; the imam of the people of Shām, al-Awzāʿī; and the imam of the jurists of the people of hadith, al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him), and Ibn al-Mundhir chose it. Also, the three days are distinguished by being the days of Minā, the days of stoning (al-ramy), and the days of tashriq, and fasting on them is forbidden. So they are siblings in these rulings; how then do they differ in the permissibility of slaughter without a text or consensus? It is narrated through two different chains, each strengthening the other, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "All of Minā is a place of sacrifice, and all the days of tashriq are days of slaughter." It was narrated from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, in which there is interruption, and from the hadith of Usāmah ibn Zayd, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Jābir.

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said: Usāmah ibn Zayd is trustworthy and reliable according to the people of Madinah.

On this question there are four opinions, and this is one of them.

The second: the time of slaughter is the day of sacrifice and two days after it. This is the position of Aḥmad, Mālik and Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on them). Aḥmad said: It is the saying of more than one of the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), and al-Athram reported it from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them).

The third: the time of sacrifice is one day only. This is the saying of Ibn Sīrīn, because it is specifically named by this designation, which indicates that the ruling is specific to it. Had it applied to three days, it would have been called "the days of sacrifice" just as the days are called "the days of stoning," "the days of Minā," and "the days of tashriq." Also, the ʿĪd is attributed to the sacrifice, and it is one day, just as one says ʿĪd al-Fiṭr.

The fourth: the saying of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Jābir ibn Zayd: it is one day in the cities, and three days in Minā, because there are the days of performing the rites (manāsik) there, such as stoning, circumambulation and shaving, so they were days for slaughter, unlike the people of the cities.

[Section: Matters Related to the Sacrifice]

Section

And from his guidance (ﷺ): "Whoever intends to sacrifice and the ten days have begun, let him not take anything from his hair or his skin."

This prohibition is established in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

As for al-Dāraquṭnī, he said: In my view the sound report is that it is mawqūf (halted) upon Umm Salamah.

And it was from his guidance (ﷺ) to choose the sacrificial animal and prefer what is fine, and that it be free from defects. "And he forbade sacrificing an animal with a missing ear or horn," meaning one whose ear is cut or whose horn is broken, a half or more. This was mentioned by Abū Dāwūd. "And he commanded that the eye and ear be examined," meaning one looks at their soundness, and that one not sacrifice one that is one-eyed, nor a muqābalah, nor a mudābarah, nor a sharqāʾ, nor a kharqāʾ. The muqābalah is the one whose front part of the ear is cut, the mudābarah is the one whose back part of the ear is cut, the sharqāʾ is the one whose ear is split, and the kharqāʾ is the one whose ear is pierced. Abū Dāwūd mentioned this.

And he also mentioned from him: "Four are not valid in sacrifices: the one-eyed whose blindness is evident, the sick whose illness is evident, the lame whose lameness is evident, and the broken one that cannot get up (lā tunqī), and the emaciated one that cannot get up (lā tunqī)," meaning from its thinness, having no marrow.

He also mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "forbade the muṣfarrah, the mustaʾṣalah, the bakhqāʾ, the mushayyaʿah, and the kasrāʾ." The muṣfarrah is the one whose ear is removed until its ear canal appears; the mustaʾṣalah is the one whose horn has been completely removed from its root; the bakhqāʾ is the one whose eye has been put out; the mushayyaʿah is the one that does not follow the flock due to thinness and weakness; the kasrāʾ is the broken one. And Allah knows best.

[He (ﷺ) Would Sacrifice at the Muṣallā]

And it was from his guidance (ﷺ) that he would sacrifice at the muṣallā. Abū Dāwūd mentioned it: "From Jābir, that he witnessed with him the Aḍḥā at the muṣallā; when he finished his sermon he descended from his minbar, and a ram was brought to him, and he slaughtered it with his own hand, and said: (In the name of Allah, and Allah is greatest. This is on behalf of me and on behalf of whoever among my ummah did not sacrifice.)" And in the Ṣaḥīḥayn it is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) "would slaughter and sacrifice at the muṣallā."

(Section: On the Combination of ʿAqīqah and Udhiyah)

Al-Khallāl said: Chapter on what is narrated that the udhiyah suffices in place of the ʿaqīqah.

ʿAbd al-Malik al-Maymūnī informed us that he said to Abū ʿAbd Allah: May it be permissible to sacrifice on behalf of a boy in place of the ʿaqīqah? He said: I do not know. Then he said: More than one person holds this view.

I said: From the Successors (tābiʿūn)? He said: Yes.

ʿAbd al-Malik also informed me in another place, he said: Abū ʿAbd Allah mentioned that some of them said: If he sacrifices, it suffices in place of the ʿaqīqah.

ʿIṣmah ibn ʿIṣām informed us, Ḥanbal related to us that Abū ʿAbd Allah said: I hope that the udhiyah suffices in place of the ʿaqīqah, if Allah wills, for one who has not had an ʿaqīqah.

ʿIṣmah ibn ʿIṣām informed me in another place, he said: Ḥanbal related to us that Abū ʿAbd Allah said: If he sacrifices on his behalf, the udhiyah suffices for him from the ʿaqīqah. He said: I saw Abū ʿAbd Allah buy a sacrificial animal, which he slaughtered on his behalf and on behalf of his family, and his son ʿAbd Allah was young; he slaughtered it, I think he intended thereby both the ʿaqīqah and the udhiyah, and distributed the meat and ate from it.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Aḥmad informed us, he said: I asked my father about the ʿaqīqah on the day of al-Aḍḥā: may it suffice to be both an udhiyah and an ʿaqīqah? He said: Either an udhiyah or an ʿaqīqah, according to what is named. This implies three narrations from Abū ʿAbd Allah:

The first: that it suffices for both.

The second: that it falls for only one of them.

The third: suspension (of judgment).

The reason it does not fall for both is that they are two slaughters for two different causes, so one slaughter does not stand for both, like the blood of tamattuʿ and the blood of expiation (fidyah). The reason for sufficiency is that the purpose of both is achieved by one slaughter, since the udhiyah on behalf of a newborn is legislated just as the ʿaqīqah is for him. So if he sacrifices and intends that it be both an ʿaqīqah and an udhiyah, it falls for both, just as if he prays two rakʿahs intending both the greeting of the masjid and the sunnah of the obligatory prayer, or if after tawaf he prays an obligatory or sunnah prayer, it counts for both it and the two rakʿahs of tawaf. Likewise, if the one performing tamattuʿ or qirān slaughters a sheep on the day of sacrifice, it suffices for the blood of tamattuʿ and for the udhiyah. And Allah knows best.

(Section)

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to Makkah, the Quraysh said: "Do you not see this stunted one cut off from his people? He claims that he is better than us, while we are the people of the pilgrimage, the people of the key-keeping (al-sidanah), and the people of the water-supplying (al-siqayah)." He said: "You are better." So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.﴾

He said: And this was revealed concerning him: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in jibt and taghut and say of those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who have believed in the way.﻿"﴾ [al-Nisa': 51] up to His words: ﴿a helper.﴾

[Section: The reason for the Prophet's specific permission to Abu Burdah ibn Niyar to sacrifice a female goat (ʿanaq) without it counting against others]

As for his (ﷺ) specifying Abu Burdah ibn Niyar with the validity of sacrificing a ʿanaq rather than anyone after him, this too had a particular reason. He had slaughtered before the prayer, interpreting (mutaʾawwilan) and not knowing that it was not valid. When the Prophet (ﷺ) informed him that this was not a sacrificial animal but merely a meat sheep, he wished to repeat the sacrifice, but he had nothing with him except a ʿanaq, which was dearer to him than two meat sheep. So he (ﷺ) granted him leave to sacrifice it, because he was excused, having previously slaughtered under an interpretation, and he was excused by his interpretation. All of this was before the ruling was firmly established. Once the ruling became firmly established, after that nothing would be valid except what conformed to the established Shariah. And success is from Allah.
